questions.questionText: When was the Union of South Africa established?
questions.explanation: Union of South Africa was created on 31 May 1910 by uniting the Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River Colony.

questions.questionText: Which four colonies were united to form South Africa?

options.text: Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River Colony

questions.explanation: The Union united four British colonies: Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange River Colony under one government.

questions.questionText: Who became the first Prime Minister of South Africa?
questions.explanation: Louis Botha, a former Boer War general, became the first Prime Minister in 1910.

questions.questionText: What type of government did the Union have?
questions.explanation: The Union operated as a British dominion with parliamentary democracy and Westminster system.

questions.questionText: Which provinces were created in the Union?

options.text: Cape of Good Hope, Natal, Transvaal, Orange Free State

questions.explanation: Four provinces were established: Cape of Good Hope, Natal, Transvaal, and Orange Free State.

questions.questionText: Who was the British monarch during the formation of the Union?
questions.explanation: King Edward VII was on the British throne when South Africa was formed, though he died in 1910.

questions.questionText: What was Natives Land Act of 1913?

options.text: Restricted African land ownership to specific areas
Divided land equally between all groups

questions.explanation: The Natives Land Act restricted African land ownership to only 7% of South Africa's land area.

questions.questionText: What were the main motivations for creating the Union?

options.text: Economic unity, defense coordination, and post-war reconciliation

questions.explanation: The Union was driven by economic integration needs, military coordination, and reconciliation between British and Boers.

questions.questionText: What was the role of Jan Smuts in early Union politics?

options.text: Served as Prime Minister and key policy architect

questions.explanation: Jan Smuts served as Prime Minister from 1919-1924 and played crucial role in drafting Union policies.

questions.questionText: What was the Native Affairs Act of 1920?

options.text: Established separate representative bodies for Africans

questions.explanation: The Act created advisory Native Representatives selected by the government rather than elected by Africans.

questions.questionText: How were black South Africans excluded from political power in the Union?

options.text: Through property qualifications and separate voter rolls
They were given full voting rights

questions.explanation: While Cape Africans could vote under property qualifications, other provinces had no African representation and later unified exclusion was implemented.

questions.questionText: What was the impact of the 1913 Natives Land Act on Africans?
questions.explanation: The Act confined Africans to limited areas, disrupting communities and forcing many into labor markets.

questions.questionText: What was the relationship between the Union government and British imperial policy?

options.text: Semi-autonomous but aligned with British interests

questions.explanation: As a British dominion, the Union controlled domestic affairs but followed British foreign policy, including WWI participation.

questions.questionText: How did South Africa participate in World War I?

options.text: Campaigns against German colonies in Africa

questions.explanation: South Africa captured German South West Africa and supported British war effort, with Botha and Smuts commanding campaigns.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the extent to which the Union of South Africa represented reconciliation between Boers and British.

options.text: Reconciliation was limited to white groups while excluding Africans

questions.explanation: White unity was achieved at the expense of African rights, consolidating white supremacy across all groups.

questions.questionText: Analyze how the Union's founding documents institutionalized racial discrimination.

options.text: Through exclusion clauses and delegated segregation powers

questions.explanation: The South Africa Act allowed provinces to maintain separate franchise rules, enabling systematic racial exclusion.

questions.questionText: To what extent was the Union a compromise between British and Boer interests?

options.text: Compromise maintained white unity but marginalized Africans
Was not a compromise at all

questions.explanation: Botha-Smuts faction and Hertzog's Nationalists shared power, creating a unified white political framework.

questions.questionText: Analyze the economic policies of the early Union government.

options.text: Mining-based economy with labor policies favoring white workers

questions.explanation: Government policies supported mining capital while using tariffs and labor laws to maintain white employment.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of Union-era racial policies for later apartheid legislation.
multiple-choice

options.text: Established precedents for later segregation and apartheid laws

questions.explanation: The Natives Land Act, pass laws, and discrimination provided legal framework that apartheid would expand.

questions.questionText: How did the formation of the Union affect South Africa's international position?

options.text: Created a significant regional power with imperial ties

questions.hint: Colonial administration and League of Nations.
questions.explanation: The Union gained control over South West Africa and became a founding member of the League of Nations.
